body.text: Beyond Chemical Isp: The Thermodynamic Case for Fission

Chemical rocketry is bound by the fundamental bond energies of molecular propellants, hitting an asymptotic specific impulse ceiling of approximately 450 seconds. Nuclear thermal propulsion (NTP) shatters this barrier by using a compact fission reactor core to superheat liquid hydrogen propellant directly to over 2,700 Kelvin. Because exhaust velocity scales inversely with the square root of molecular mass, pure hydrogen yields specific impulses exceeding 900 seconds.

items: High Specific Impulse: NTP systems deliver twice the propellant efficiency of modern cryogenic hydrolox rocket engines.
Shortened Transit Windows: Doubling exhaust velocity reduces Earth-Mars transit durations from nine months down to fewer than one hundred days.
HALEU Fuel Cores: High-assay low-enriched uranium (under 20% enrichment) coated with refractory zirconium carbide ensures structural stability under extreme thermal flux.
Abort Flexibility: Vastly increased delta-v budgets permit opposition-class trajectories with immediate return capabilities.

body.text: Chemical engines carried humanity to the Moon; nuclear thermal propulsion is the inescapable thermodynamic prerequisite for becoming a true interplanetary civilization.

body.text: Reactor Core Neutronics and Cryogenic Liquid Hydrogen Expansion

Modern NTP designs leverage beryllium oxide neutron reflectors and rotating control drums with boron carbide poison segments to govern reactivity. Liquid hydrogen stored at 20 Kelvin acts as both regenerative coolant and reaction mass, absorbing gigawatts of thermal energy across millimeter-scale propellant channels without chemical combustion.

body.text: Interplanetary Orbit Transfer Windows and Radiation Shielding

Shadow shielding using layered tungsten, lithium hydride, and depleted propellant tanks attenuates core gamma rays and neutrons to levels lower than the natural cosmic ray background absorbed during long-duration interplanetary cruise phases.
